title: Pair Key
statement: Implement `solve(rows, user, day)`. `rows` is a list of `[user, day, score]`. Build a lookup keyed by the pair `(user, day)` and return the score for the requested pair. If the pair is absent, return the string `none`. Later rows overwrite the same pair.
hints: Use a tuple (user, day) as the dict key. A list cannot be a key.
Insert rows from left to right so the last score wins.
A missing key returns the string none.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A tuple of the two fields is hashable and distinguishes (a, b) from (b, a).

editorial: A tuple of the two fields is hashable and distinguishes (a, b) from (b, a). A list is not a key. The lookup is then one dict get. Last write wins when the same user and day appear twice.
